Assemble the results of a bundle run on a cluster

Source: R/hpc.R
collect_hpc.Rd

Assembles the results of the tasks of a bundle written by write_hpc_bundle(), once its folder results/ has been copied back from the cluster, into what fit_hazard_models() returns: the fits, their cross-validation results and a summary of one row per model, ready for hazard_weights() and the functions that average models.

Usage

collect_hpc(dir = ".")

Arguments

dir

A character vector, the folder of the bundle, on your own computer, with the folder results/ copied back into it, or the folders of the bundle and of its rounds. Defaults to the working folder.

Value

A list with the four elements that fit_hazard_models() returns: fits, loo, kfold and summary. In summary, round is the round each model's result comes from (1 for the first bundle), status is "fitted", "failed" or "missing", and seconds is the time each fit and its cross-validation took on the cluster.

Details

Given the folders of a bundle and of its rounds, written by next_hpc_round(), it assembles each model from its latest round, the last round that fitted it, whether the result of that round is there, failed or missing, so that a model fitted again is never given its earlier fit without a word. The folders must be the first bundle and every round from the second to the last, all holding the same data, and can be given in any order.

Nothing is assembled from a bundle whose files have changed since it was written, or with a result computed from another bundle: the files are checked against their checksums, and each result against the stamp of the bundle that computed it.

The sampling rule of the bundle is applied to each fit and reported as fit_hazard_models() reports it. A model whose fit failed is reported with its reason, and one whose fit has no result yet (its task did not run, or has not finished) is marked "missing" in the summary and named in a warning, so the results can be looked at before every task is done. A model is cross-validated by refitting only when every one of its folds has a result with a log predictive density defined for each of its units; otherwise the reason is given in the summary. A density of zero, a log predictive density of -Inf, is kept, as kfold_hazard() keeps it.

See also

write_hpc_bundle(), which writes the bundle, and hpc_status(), which says what each task has done.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# on your own computer, once results/ has been copied back into the bundle
out <- collect_hpc("my-run")
out$summary
weights <- hazard_weights(out$kfold)

# with the round written by next_hpc_round() for a model that did not converge
out <- collect_hpc(c("my-run", "my-run-round-2"))
} # }
